I'm trying to figure out the wall/mirror rule by comparing examples: in one case a colored dot near a wall column ends up duplicated both at the end of its row and at another position, so I'm testing whether the offset relates to the dot's distance from the wall.

Looking at examples 1 and 2, the pattern seems consistent -- two dots appear at the last column, one in the original row and one in the row above it. But example 4 breaks that pattern with a dot at row 0 instead, so I'm re-checking the grid to see what's actually different about this case.

Checking each example: in ex2 with row7 as a gap row, it moves right to col14 with a second mark at row6 col14. But in ex3 and ex4, the row containing the object actually has a 5 blocking it, so it seems to stop earlier and pair with a mark at row0 instead — suggesting when blocked, the piece behaves differently, maybe bouncing diagonally toward the top.

Working through ex3 more carefully: from (6,9) it hits the wall at (6,10), then reflects diagonally upward-right, tracing through (5,11),(4,12),(3,13),(2,14),(1,15) until reaching row0 at (0,16). That matches the diagonal reflection theory, so now I need to figure out what the second mark at (6,27) represents.

Testing this against ex4: the 6 at (4,1) hits the wall at (4,3), then goes diagonally up-right through (3,4),(2,5),(1,6) to land at (0,7) -- consistent again. There's also a second mark at (4,10), which is just the straight-line continuation to the row's end.

Checking against ex1, the unblocked case: the dot at (5,17) passes through a gap and exits straight at (5,19), while a second diagonal ray starting at (5,18) moves up-right to (4,19), hitting the right edge. So it seems each ball produces two rays -- one straight, one diagonal -- and only their exit points get marked.

Now I need to apply this rule to the actual test input.
